arxiv-1706-06782.title: Object Detection Using Deep CNNs Trained on Synthetic Images
arxiv-1706-06782.creator: P. S. Rajpura, H. Bojinov, R. S. Hegde
arxiv-1706-06782.description: Abstract The need for large annotated image datasets for training Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) has been a significant impediment for their adoption in computer vision applications. We show that with transfer learning an effective object detector can be trained almost entirely on synthetically rendered datasets. We apply this strategy for detecting packaged food products clustered in refrigerator scenes.

arxiv-2009-03380.title: Chance-Constrained Optimal Distribution Network Partitioning to Enhance Grid Resilience
arxiv-2009-03380.creator: Shuchismita Biswas, Manish K. Singh, and Virgilio A. Centeno
arxiv-2009-03380.description: Abstract This paper formulates a chance-constrained optimal distribution network partitioning (ODNP) problem addressing uncertainties in load and renewable energy generation; and presents a solution methodology using sample average approximation (SAA). The objective is to identify potential sub-networks in the existing distribution grid; that are likely to survive as self-adequate islands if supply from the main grid is lost.

arxiv-2105-10288.title: Extremely Lightweight Quantization Robust Real-Time Single-Image Super Resolution for Mobile Devices
arxiv-2105-10288.creator: Mustafa Ayazoglu Aselsan Research Ankara, Turkey mayazoglu@aselsan.com.tr
arxiv-2105-10288.description: Abstract Single-Image Super Resolution (SISR) is a classical computer vision problem and it has been studied for over decades. With the recent success of deep learning methods, recent work on SISR focuses solutions with deep learning methodologies and achieves state-of-the-art results. However most of the state-of-the-art SISR methods contain millions of parameters and layers, which limits their practical applications.

arxiv-2203-03058.title: Relaxed Paxos: Quorum Intersection Revisited (Again) Conference: 9th Workshop on Principles and Practice of Consistency for Distributed Data ; April 5–8, 2022; RENNES, France 9th Workshop on Principles and Practice of Consistency for Distributed Data (PaPoC’22), April 5–8, 2022, RENNES, France DOI:
arxiv-2203-03058.creator: Heidi Howard, Richard Mortier
arxiv-2203-03058.description: Abstract . Distributed consensus, the ability to reach agreement in the face of failures, is a fundamental primitive for constructing reliable distributed systems. The Paxos algorithm is synonymous with consensus and widely utilized in production. Paxos uses two phases: phase one and phase two, each requiring a quorum of acceptors, to reach consensus during a round of the protocol.

arxiv-2204-13881.creator: Yi Qin, Yang Wang, Yi Li, Jian Li
arxiv-2204-13881.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yi Qin, Yang Wang, Yi Li, Jian Li. In this report, we propose a new adaptive time filter algorithm for the unsteady Stokes/Darcy model. First we present a first order θ \theta -scheme with the variable time step which is one parameter family of Linear Multi-step methods and use a time filter algorithm to increase the convergence order to second order with almost no increasing the amount of computation. Furthermore, we construct coupled and decoupled adaptive algorithms.

arxiv-2205-12641.title: Flavon Signatures at the HL-LHC
arxiv-2205-12641.creator: M. A. Arroyo-Ureña, Amit Chakraborty, J. Lorenzo Díaz-Cruz, Dilip Kumar Ghosh, Najimuddin Khan, Stefano Moretti
arxiv-2205-12641.description: Abstract The detection of a single Higgs boson at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has allowed one to probe some properties of it, including the Yukawa and gauge couplings. However, in order to probe the Higgs potential, one has to rely on new production mechanisms, such as Higgs pair production.

arxiv-2309-12918.title: Combining Resonant and Tail-based Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2309-12918.creator: Gerrit Bickendorf, Manuel Drees, Gregor Kasieczka, Claudius Krause, David Shih
arxiv-2309-12918.description: Abstract In many well-motivated models of the electroweak scale, cascade decays of new particles can result in highly boosted hadronic resonances (e.g. Z / W / h Z/W/h ). This can make these models rich and promising targets for recently developed resonant anomaly detection methods powered by modern machine learning.

arxiv-2406-09510.title: Topologically Robust Quantum Network Nonlocality
arxiv-2406-09510.creator: Sadra Boreiri, Tamas Krivachy, Pavel Sekatski, Antoine Girardin, Nicolas Brunner
arxiv-2406-09510.description: Abstract We discuss quantum network Bell nonlocality in a setting where the network structure is not fully known. More concretely, an honest user may trust their local network topology, but not the structure of the rest of the network, involving distant (and potentially dishonest) parties.

arxiv-2512-10345.title: Estimating stellar atmospheric parameters and elemental abundances using fully connected residual network
arxiv-2512-10345.creator: Shuo Li, Yin-Bi Li ∗, A-Li Luo ∗, Jun-Chao Liang ∗, Hai-Ling Lu, Hugh R. A. Jones
arxiv-2512-10345.description: Abstract Stellar atmospheric parameters and elemental abundances are traditionally determined using template matching techniques based on high-resolution spectra. However, these methods are sensitive to noise and unsuitable for ultra-low-resolution data. Given that the Chinese Space Station Telescope (CSST) will acquire large volumes of ultra-low-resolution spectra, developing effective methods for ultra-low-resolution spectral analysis is crucial.

pmc-13219879.title: Air Everywhere: A Rare Post-ERCP Syndrome of Acute Pancreatitis, Pneumothorax, and Multicompartment Air Leak without Perforation
pmc-13219879.creator: Antonio Al Hazzouri, Maria Ziade, Katherine Atallah, Mandy El Khoury, Julie Bechara, Philippe Attieh, Pierre Mourad
pmc-13219879.description: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a widely used therapeutic procedure for pancreatobiliary disorders but is associated with a range of complications, most commonly post-ERCP pancreatitis (PEP). Post-ERCP air leak syndromes—including pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, pneumoperitoneum, and subcutaneous emphysema—are exceptionally rare, particularly in the absence of an identifiable gastrointestinal perforation.

pmc-13487272.title: Click-code-seq protocol for genome-wide single-nucleotide-resolution mapping of major types of DNA modifications
pmc-13487272.creator: Lucie Lefevre, Emilie A. Aghajani, Navnit K. Singh, Livia Maria Anna Pietrow, Nikolai J.L. Püllen, Vakil Takhaveev, Shana J. Sturla
pmc-13487272.description: SummaryDNA modifications are central to carcinogenesis, chemotherapy drug action, neurodegeneration, and aging. Here, we present a protocol for click-code-seq, a next-generation sequencing technique for genome-wide single-nucleotide-resolution mapping of major types of DNA modifications: oxidized guanines and abasic sites. We describe steps for genomic DNA extraction and library preparation, including enzymatic modification conversion and click-chemistry-based tagging.

uslaw-usc-t43-s1471.description: United States Code, Title 43 (Public Lands); Chapter 31 (Department Of The Interior). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Appropriations for contingent expenses of the Department of the Interior shall be available, to the extent specified therein, for the payment of damages to private property (not to exceed $500 in any one case) caused by the negligent operation of motor vehicles under such.
